name: TJA1050
description: The TJA1050 is NXP's 5 V high-speed CAN physical-layer transceiver, the interface between a CAN protocol controller's TXD/RXD pins and the differential CANH/CANL bus. Like all transceivers it is a PHY, not a controller, so it pairs with an MCP2515 or an MCU's CAN peripheral to do the actual protocol work. It is the direct successor to the PCA82C250, adding very low electromagnetic emission, a TXD dominant time-out, and a silent mode, while keeping input levels compatible with 3.3 V controllers. It runs from 4.75 to 5.25 V and handles data rates from 60 kbaud up to 1 Mbaud over a wide-common-mode differential receiver. Its standout trait is the silent mode (S pin tied to VCC) that disables only the transmitter while everything else keeps running, letting a node listen without ever disturbing the bus.

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Transmit data input; reads data in from the CAN controller to the bus line drivers (LOW = dominant).

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Receive data output; reads data out from the bus lines to the CAN controller.

pins.name: Vref
pins.description: Reference voltage output at 0.5 x VCC (VCC/2), for split-termination common-mode biasing.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Select input: tie to GND for high-speed mode, tie to VCC for silent mode (transmitter disabled, all other functions active).

extra.data_rate: 60 kbaud to 1 Mbaud (the TXD dominant time-out sets the floor)
extra.txd_dominant_timeout: yes (prevents bus lock-up on stuck-dominant TXD)
extra.logic_compat: input levels compatible with 3.3 V devices

typical_application: 5 V automotive/industrial CAN node: a CAN controller (MCP2515 or MCU peripheral) drives TXD/RXD, the TJA1050 drives a 120-ohm-terminated twisted pair. Common drop-in successor to PCA82C250 designs.
gotchas: Transceiver (PHY) only - not a controller; pair with an MCP2515 or MCU CAN peripheral.
5 V part: unlike the SN65HVD230 it needs a 5 V VCC, though its TXD/RXD inputs accept 3.3 V logic from the controller side.
Has silent mode but no true low-power standby/sleep mode - it is always drawing normal supply current when powered.
S (pin 8) must be tied low (GND) for normal high-speed transmit; left floating, mode is undefined.
Bus needs external 120-ohm termination at both ends; the device does not terminate.
